draft.title: Transformations in mapping form
card: A mapping rule such as (x, y) → (2x + 1, 3y) says where each point (x, y) on a graph moves to. The first part gives the new x-value. The second part gives the new y-value.

A number multiplying x or y is a dilation. A negative sign is a reflection. A number added or subtracted is a translation. A factor of 2 on x dilates from the y-axis by a factor of 2 (parallel to the x-axis).
The y-part changes the y-coordinate. A factor of 3 on y dilates from the x-axis by a factor of 3. A y-part of −y reflects in the x-axis. An x-part of −x reflects in the y-axis.
Worked example: apply (x, y) → (2x + 1, 3y) to the point (4, 5). New x = 2 × 4 + 1 = 9. New y = 3 × 5 = 15. The point moves to (9, 15).
draft.remember: Read a mapping rule as new x, then new y, and apply it to each point.

a.q: The rule (x, y) → (2x + 1, 3y) is applied to the point (3, −2). Where does the point move to?
a.why: New x = 2 × 3 + 1 = 7. New y = 3 × (−2) = −6. The point moves to (7, −6). (8, −6) comes from adding 1 before doubling, which is the wrong order, since the rule doubles x and then adds 1.
a.clue: Double x first, then add 1, and multiply y by 3.

b.q: Which mapping rule reflects a graph in the x-axis and then translates it 4 units to the left? (Apply the reflection first.)
b.why: Reflecting in the x-axis changes y to −y and leaves x alone. Moving 4 units left subtracts 4 from x, so the rule is (x − 4, −y). (x + 4, −y) moves the graph to the right, which is the tempting sign mistake.
b.clue: Reflection in the x-axis changes the y-part only. Left means x gets smaller.

problems.detail: The card says only that an added or subtracted number is a translation. It never says which direction it moves the graph (subtracting from x moves it left), so question b needs more than the card teaches. Only the clue supplies it.

check.summary: Both questions and explanations are correct. The only gap is that the card never says which way an added or subtracted number moves the graph, which question b relies on.

final.title: Transformations in mapping form
card: A mapping rule such as \((x, y) \to (2x + 1, 3y)\) says where each point \((x, y)\) on a graph moves to. The first part gives the new x-value. The second part gives the new y-value.

A number multiplying a part is a dilation: \(2x\) dilates from the y-axis by a factor of 2, and \(3y\) dilates from the x-axis by a factor of 3. A negative sign is a reflection: \(-y\) reflects in the x-axis and \(-x\) reflects in the y-axis.

A number added or subtracted is a translation. In the x-part, \(x + 1\) moves the graph 1 unit right and \(x - 4\) moves it 4 units left. In the y-part, \(y + 2\) moves it 2 units up and \(y - 2\) moves it 2 units down.
Worked example: apply \((x, y) \to (2x + 1, 3y)\) to the point \((4, 5)\). New \(x = 2 \times 4 + 1 = 9\). New \(y = 3 \times 5 = 15\). The point moves to \((9, 15)\).
final.remember: Read a mapping rule as new \(x\), then new \(y\), and apply it to each point.

a.q: The rule \((x, y) \to (2x + 1, 3y)\) is applied to the point \((3, -2)\). Where does the point move to?
a.why: New \(x = 2 \times 3 + 1 = 7\). New \(y = 3 \times (-2) = -6\). The point moves to \((7, -6)\). \((8, -6)\) comes from adding 1 before doubling, which is the wrong order, since the rule doubles \(x\) and then adds 1.
a.clue: Double \(x\) first, then add 1, and multiply \(y\) by 3.

b.q: Which mapping rule reflects a graph in the x-axis and then translates it 4 units to the left? (Apply the reflection first.)
b.why: Reflecting in the x-axis changes \(y\) to \(-y\) and leaves \(x\) alone. Moving 4 units left subtracts 4 from \(x\), so the rule is \((x, y) \to (x - 4, -y)\). The rule \((x, y) \to (x + 4, -y)\) moves the graph 4 units right, which is the tempting sign mistake.
b.clue: Reflection in the x-axis changes the y-part only.
